item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it leaves the lower-level Add implementation unchanged and adds the requested buffered Upload API. It still needs revision before merge, chiefly to delegate Upload to Add and strengthen error/retry tests.","reasons":["A preserves Add's existing behavior; B changes it to eagerly buffer every caller-built multipart body, altering memory, streaming, and error semantics contrary to the contract.","Both reuse internal/multipartbody.NewFile and correctly encode the file field, filename, and content.","A tests filename/content validation, while B does not test validation at all.","B has the stronger streamed-content retry test because it uploads from os.Open; A only uses bytes.NewReader in its retry test despite the contract explicitly requesting streamed-content coverage. This testing advantage does not outweigh B's production API behavior change."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","There is no source-reader failure test.","The retry test does not use a one-shot or file-backed reader, so streamed-content behavior is not directly demonstrated."],"risks_b":["Add now eagerly reads and buffers arbitrary custom multipart bodies, violating the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and potentially causing substantial memory use or changed read-error timing.","Upload calls a new private add helper rather than the existing FilesService.Add method, violating the required delegation path even though request logic is shared.","There are no validation or source-reader-error tests required by the contract, and the extra Add retry test primarily verifies the out-of-scope Add behavior change."]}
